dedupe_keys.name: multi rat wireless network simulator 4g 5g and satellite

description: The Multi-RAT wireless network simulator models resource allocation across 4G, 5G and satellite access networks without simulating protocol details, developed at Sapienza University of Rome by Emanuele De Santis, Alessandro Giuseppi, Antonio Pietrabissa and Francesco Delli Priscoli within the European project on integrating satellite and cellular networks (5G-ALLSTAR). User equipment requests a bit rate from one or more access points without knowing their type; each access point computes the resources to allocate (resource blocks for LTE and NR, symbols for satellite) from path loss and inter-cell interference; users and drone base stations can move. Coverage: generic synthetic scenarios. Format and access: Python source on Zenodo (first release April 2020, version 0.2 in October 2021) and on GitHub as trunk96/wireless-network-simulator-v2, free under Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 for the first deposit. Caveats: abstracts away protocols and data transmission; small research team. Simulation uses: capacity planning of combined terrestrial and satellite access, and resilience studies where a technology fails and users move to another. Related records: ns-3 and Simu5G give protocol-level simulation.
